title: Adaptive Keyframe Sampling for Long Video Understanding (AKS)
grouping: Recursive equal temporal bisection; query relevance controls whether recursion continues
allocation: Compare top-M mean relevance against all-frame mean; split frame budget between child bins when concentration is below threshold
within_selection: Top relevance frames when recursion terminates
overlap_with_current_D: Training-free fixed-budget relevance and temporal coverage; establishes a stronger baseline than Uniform
comparison_priority: High: direct selector baseline with both original and matched-scorer settings
limitations: Does not use the same content-change boundaries as D; distinguish matched-embedding ablation from full original-method reproduction

title: QCA: Query- and Content-Aware Keyframe Selection for Long Video Understanding
evidence_level: Primary full paper; official program https://eccv.ecva.net/virtual/2026/poster/4927 and author code https://github.com/hktk07/QCA verified
grouping: Uniform temporal segments; default segment count 12
allocation: Segment mean image-text matching plus content deviation and variance determine quotas
within_selection: Most relevant anchor; relevance-filtered greedy visual-diversity selection
overlap_with_current_D: Segment scoring, adaptive quota allocation and within-segment selection closely overlap D framework
limitations: Content-aware boundaries alone do not establish novelty; original scorer/FPS and modified common-scorer comparisons must be distinguished; local reproduction not yet completed

title: VideoTree: Adaptive Tree-based Video Representation for LLM Reasoning on Long Videos
grouping: Visual K-means clusters recursively refined; clusters need not be temporally contiguous
allocation: Caption-based LLM relevance guides breadth expansion and depth refinement
within_selection: Centroid-nearest frames at tree nodes are captioned; captions ordered temporally for reasoning
overlap_with_current_D: Query-adaptive hierarchical grouping and finer detail for relevant groups are established ideas
comparison_priority: Medium: related mechanism and system-cost comparison
limitations: Caption-to-LLM pipeline differs from direct image QA; equal selected-frame count does not equal equal total computation

title: E-VRAG: Enhancing Long Video Understanding with Resource-Efficient Retrieval Augmented Generation
publication_status: arXiv version 2508.01546; peer-reviewed acceptance not verified
grouping: Groups temporally adjacent similar frames; later retrieval groups using lightweight VLM output distributions
allocation: Group quotas proportional to group frame count; query decomposition and lightweight scoring precede retrieval
within_selection: Within-group inverse-transform relevance sampling; multi-view QA after retrieval
overlap_with_current_D: Contiguous groups preserve separate temporal occurrences and address redundant high-scoring frames
comparison_priority: Medium-high: close grouping mechanism; compare selector separately from full system
limitations: Contains extra scoring and QA stages; primary experiment must count their costs and avoid attributing multi-view QA gains solely to frame grouping

title: Focus: Efficient Keyframe Selection for Long Video Understanding
publication_status: arXiv version 2510.27280; peer-reviewed acceptance not verified
grouping: Fixed-length clips treated as bandit arms
allocation: Coarse-to-fine exploration guided by empirical relevance means and confidence bounds; equal frame quotas among chosen clips
within_selection: Section 2.4 describes relevance-weighted sampling without replacement after nearest-neighbor score interpolation
overlap_with_current_D: Region selection before frame selection; generic uncertainty-aware exploration is already studied
comparison_priority: Medium: useful for end-to-end cost and candidate-scoring efficiency
limitations: Keep region-scoring budget distinct from final QA token budget; abstract top-scoring description is less precise than the within-selection details in Section 2.4

title: Wavelet-based Frame Selection by Detecting Semantic Boundary for Long Video Understanding (WFS-SB)
evidence_level: Primary full paper; verified by coordinating audit
grouping: At 1 fps, query-conditioned BLIP-2 ITM score sequence; db4 wavelet coarsest-detail coefficients detect semantic boundaries
allocation: Softmax of composite segment importance allocates budget
overlap_with_current_D: Semantic boundaries, segment importance, softmax budget allocation and within-segment selection are a very close match in overall structure
comparison_priority: Very high: closest direct baseline and novelty audit
limitations: Current D uses query-independent CLIP content-change boundaries; must isolate that distinction rather than claiming boundary-based adaptive sampling itself is new

title: Video-Seer: A Hierarchical Scene Selection and Multi-View Analysis
publication_status: IEEE Transactions on Multimedia, 2026; DOI 10.1109/TMM.2026.3673555; institutional record dated 2026-03-12
evidence_level: Author institutional publication record and abstract; full text not accessed
grouping: Dynamic scene segmentation reported in abstract
allocation: Relevance-based adaptive frame quotas reported in abstract
within_selection: Fine local grids plus global view reported in abstract
overlap_with_current_D: Same-journal precedent combines dynamic segmentation, relevance allocation and multiple visual views
comparison_priority: Very high for full-text related-work verification; direct baseline feasibility pending
limitations: Do not infer exact boundary algorithm, quota formula, evaluation setup or reproducibility from abstract alone

title: Can I Trust Your Answer? Visually Grounded Video Question Answering (NExT-GQA)
evidence_level: Primary official paper page; grounding benchmark verified by coordinating audit
grouping: Not a frame-grouping method; temporal evidence annotations support grounding evaluation
overlap_with_current_D: Supports measuring evidence grounding separately from QA correctness; approximately 10.5K grounding annotations
comparison_priority: High: grounding evaluation reference and possible complementary benchmark
limitations: Not a long-video equivalent; cannot substitute its results for long-video generalization or assume its temporal annotations establish frame-level evidence sufficiency
